title: poreTransport operation

pointTable.title: Per J_v point and ion: what the pore did
pointTable.definitions: R_obs = 1 - c_perm/c_bulk (observed, against the bulk feed); R_real = 1 - c_perm/c_wall (real, against the wall, past the polarisation film).

pointTables.title: Per J_v point and ion: why the pore held it back -- the partition at each face
pointTables.definitions: Just inside each face the pore holds the solution's concentration times a PARTITION: c_pore(0)/c_wall at the feed face, c_pore(1)/c_perm at the permeate face, each equal to Phi_S x Born x gamma ratio x Donnan, the factors the law used (the partitions are read off the solved pore; a gate holds the product).  lambda = r_i/r_p (r_i the radius the ion's species record carries).  Phi_S = (1 - lambda)^2, the steric partition.  K_d, K_c: the hindrance of diffusion and of convection inside the pore (Dechadilok & Deen 2006).  Born = exp(-dW_i/kT), the dielectric exclusion, the same at both faces (1 when eps_p = eps_b).  gamma ratio: the activity ratio the declared `activity` carries across the face (1 under ideal).  Donnan = exp(-z_i F dpsi_D/RT), dpsi_D the face's Donnan jump: below 1 for a co-ion (the sign of the fixed charge), above 1 for a counter-ion.  Pe = K_c J_v / (K_d D_i A_k/dx), convection against hindered diffusion across the pore.  A feed-face partition below 1 holds an ion back at the entrance, but the REJECTION is not that factor alone: it is set by both faces and by the transport between them, and in a mixture it need not move one way with J_v.  An ion as large as the pore (lambda >= 1) is EXCLUDED: Phi_S 0, both partitions 0, no pore value.

pointTables.title: Per J_v point: the potential across the membrane, step by step, and the pore's numerics
pointTables.definitions: psi is relative to the feed-side solution at the wall (psi_m = 0).  Feed Donnan jump = psi(0), from that solution into the pore's first node; pore = psi(1) - psi(0), the potential the ions build inside the pore; permeate Donnan jump = psi_p - psi(1); the three sum to dPsi_m = psi_p, the potential difference across the membrane (Geraldes & Alves 2008, Table 2; a gate holds the sum).  ||F|| is the station Newton's final residual -- the 2-norm of its rows, each normalised by the terms it balances -- and the tolerance it had to meet.  Electroneutrality (the worst node's |sum z c + X_d| / (sum |z| c + |X_d|)), zero current (|sum z N| / sum |z N|) and flux constancy (each interval's flux against J_v c_perm, relative to the two terms it nets) are MEASURED on the answer: round-off when the equations are satisfied.  Stiffness: the largest electromigration flux against the net flux, a property of the answer, not of the grid.  Converging is not a verdict: these say the equations were solved, not that the model fits a membrane.

description:
The PROPS BENCH of the DSPM-DE transport law at IMPOSED permeate fluxes: the same TransportModel the spiral-wound module marches, built through the same factory, the same `transportParameters` reader and the same wall kernel, handed J_v instead of closing J_w = A_w (dP - dpi) -- the way NanoFiltran (Geraldes & Alves 2008) takes it. Publishes per J_v point p and per ion species c_bulk__p

, c_wall__p

, c_perm__p

(mol/m3), Rreal__p

= 1 - c_perm/c_wall and Robs__p

= 1 - c_perm/c_bulk, and permeateCharge_max; where the pore was solved also dPsi_m_V_p

(the potential difference across the membrane as Geraldes & Alves 2008 define it: the permeate's potential against the feed-side solution at the wall, both Donnan jumps included, CODATA volts) and poreNewton_p

/ poreContinuations_p

(the station's Newton iterations; the first point from the seed, each later one warm-started) and poreNodes_p

; WHY each ion was held back (DEV.md 4c C165): per ion lambda_, Kd_, Kc_, PhiS_, bornFactor_ (once per op) and per point Pe__p

, the activity ratio, Donnan factor and partition at each face (gammaRatioFeed_/donnanFeed_/partitionFeed__p

, gammaRatioPerm_/donnanPerm_/partitionPerm__p

) and the pore's face concentrations c_poreFeed_/c_porePerm__p

; per point the three potential steps psiDonnanFeed_V_p

+ psiPore_V_p

+ psiDonnanPerm_V_p

= dPsi_m_V_p

, permeateCharge_p

, and the numerics poreResidual_p

against poreTolerance, poreElectroneutral_p

, poreCurrent_p

, poreFluxConstancy_p

, poreStiffness_p

; every diagnostic carries its unit. Two named TABLES a view draws (the propsDict's `views`, or this op's defaults): `points` (one row per J_v point, the per-point diagnostics as columns) and `pore` (every point's solved c_i(x) and psi(x); the `profile` CSV is written from it), whose default views draw the ions and the potential across the pore of EVERY op, at its last J_v point. An ion as large as the pore (lambda >= 1) is EXCLUDED: no pore unknown, permeate 0, its film counted in the wall's electroneutrality (announced). Witness nanofiltran_geraldesAlves2008, the NanoFiltran paper's one case (gates check_nanofiltran_reference, check_nanofiltran_paper, check_postprocessing). The film is built from the `polarisation {}` policy directly (not buildPolarisation), because the feed is declared as salts and DSPM-DE hands the kernel each ion's own z and D.

membrane.title: Membrane record
membrane.description: A membrane record (data/standards/assets or the case's constant/assets) carrying a poreModel {} block.

chargeDensity.title: Fixed charge for this op
chargeDensity.description: Replaces the membrane record's poreModel chargeDensity (signed, mol/m3) for THIS op only, announced with both values; the record is never modified.  Its DIRECTION is the record key's (see the membrane record's chargeDensity).  For a membrane whose charge was FITTED as a function of the feed (Bowen & Mohammad's CA30, the NanoFiltran paper's Eq. 43), which no single record value can carry.  Refused on a record with no poreModel {} or a non-finite value.

transport.title: Transport law
transport.description: Only `DSPM-DE` honours an imposed J_v; any other word refuses.  Absent = DSPM-DE.

transportParameters.title: Transport-law parameters
transportParameters.description: Parameters a transport law reads for itself (the block batchDiafilter hands its law too).  `gelPolarisation` reads `gel { solute <gel-forming solute>; c_gel <kg/m3>; sieving { <solute> <S>; ... }; source "..."; }` -- S in [0, 1) for EVERY solute, and `source` says where c_g and S come from.  `DSPM-DE` reads `poreSolver { method finiteDifference; nodes <n>; grid uniform | graded | adaptive; grading <beta>; gridTolerance <cells>; gridPasses <n>; wallClosure porePermeate | solutionDiffusion; }`, `hindrance DechadilokDeen2006;`, `activity wallDavies | ideal | bulkOverPoreDavies;` and `bulkDielectric <eps>;` -- and nothing else (an unknown key or word refuses).

poreSolver.title: DSPM-DE pore solver
poreSolver.description: How DSPM-DE crosses the pore: it is SOLVED (DEV.md 4c C138; the default since 2026-10-24, the only method since C142).  Absent = `method finiteDifference;` on 101 nodes, uniform, with `wallClosure porePermeate`, each default announced.  The extended Nernst-Planck equations on `nodes` grid points across the pore (faces included), electroneutrality at every node and zero current, and -- in the SAME Newton -- the film's interface balance at the wall and the water flux J_w = A_w (dP - dpi): one Newton per station on the declared block-tridiagonal structure with an analytic Jacobian.  NanoFiltran (Geraldes & Alves 2008) is the reference it is compared with.  `nodes` defaults to 101, announced.  `grid` is `uniform` (the default, announced), `graded` (the tanh map toward both faces of `grading`, 0 < beta <= 6 -- `grading` alone means graded; MEASURED not to help: the steep region of a mixed-counter-ion pore is an interior front) or `adaptive` (DEV.md 4c C144: the nodes equidistribute the curvature of the solved potential, |psi''|^(1/3) plus its mean, re-solved until no node moves by more than `gridTolerance` of its own cell -- default 0.1 -- in at most `gridPasses` re-solves per station -- default 8 -- the grid carried station to station; MEASURED at 0.76x the uniform error on an interior front and the same error on the corpus cases, which is why it is an option and not the default).  `grading` on a uniform or adaptive grid, `graded` with no grading, and `gridTolerance`/`gridPasses` on a fixed grid each refuse by name.  `wallClosure`: `porePermeate` (default) closes the multi-ionic wall with the solved pore's own permeate; `solutionDiffusion` closes it with the salts' solution-diffusion B_s, a permeate the pore does not make.  `method closedForm;` (the default until 2026-10-24) is RETIRED and refuses by name with its reason: it did not solve the pore, and with the corrected K_d its transmission tends to K_c > 1 at low Peclet number.  An unknown method word refuses.

gridTolerance.title: Adaptive grid: node movement accepted as settled (cells)

gridPasses.title: Adaptive grid: re-solves per station, at most

hindrance.title: DSPM-DE hindrance factors
hindrance.description: Absent = `DechadilokDeen2006`, the one pair (announced as the default): K_d = H/Phi (lambda <= 0.95; 0.984((1-lambda)/lambda)^2.5 above) and K_c their rational fit -- the cross-section-averaged pair (Ind. Eng. Chem. Res. 45 (2006) 6953).  H, the Dechadilok-Deen polynomial, is Phi K_d.  `legacy` (H itself taken as K_d, so the steric partition counted twice in diffusion; the default until 2026-10-24) REFUSES by name, saying why.

activity.title: DSPM-DE activity treatment
activity.description: Absent = `wallDavies`: Davies at the bulk ionic strength on the feed face, the permeate ideal.  `ideal`: every activity coefficient 1.  `bulkOverPoreDavies`: gamma_bulk/gamma_pore at BOTH faces, Davies (log10) with A(eps, T) = 1.82483e6 (eps T)^-1.5 -- eps_b on the solution side, eps_p on the pore side, the pore gammas at the pore's end nodes; evaluated inside the station's Newton on the answer's own ionic strengths.

bulkDielectric.title: Bulk dielectric constant
bulkDielectric.description: The solution's relative dielectric constant in the Born term and in A(eps_b).  Absent = SolventProperties::epsWater(T) (78.45 at 25 C).

feedMolPerM3.title: Feed salts [mol/m3]
feedMolPerM3.description: One entry per SALT component of the package (each with `dissociatesTo`), its bulk molar concentration in mol/m3; the law decomposes the salts into ions.

J_v.title: Imposed permeate fluxes
J_v.description: The permeate (water) fluxes the bench IMPOSES, per unit MEMBRANE area, one solved point each: the law skips its J_v = A_w (dP - dpi) closure and solves the ions at each given J_v, the way NanoFiltran (Geraldes & Alves 2008) takes it as its input.  DIRECTION, at the transport level: a higher J_v raises convection against hindered diffusion inside the pore -- each ion's Peclet number Pe_i = K_c J_v / (K_d D_i A_k/dx), published per ion and point -- and raises the polarisation at the wall (c_wall/c_bulk, by the film model).  WHAT THIS DOES NOT SAY: which way a REJECTION moves.  In a mixture the observed rejection is not monotone in this parameter -- the counter-ions compete for the fixed charge across the pore, so a trace counter-ion's rejection can change sign and a co-ion can be negatively rejected (tutorials/props/membrane/nanofiltran_geraldesAlves2008: Na+ with J_v in example_ideal, Cl- beside the dye in study B).  For a given feed the answer is a run with the value changed, not a sentence.

profile.title: Pore-profile CSV
profile.description: A file name (in the case directory; never under data/standards/): every point's solved pore -- point, J_v, node, xi, x_um over the equivalent thickness dx/A_k, c_<ion>_molm3 per ion species, psi_V on the dPsi_m_V reference.  A run output, like every props CSV.  Refused when the law solved no pore.

k_film.title: Constant film coefficient
k_film.description: k for every ion, in place of `massTransfer {}` (NanoFiltran simulates "no polarisation" with 10 m/s).

massTransfer.title: Film-coefficient correlation
massTransfer.description: The cell's correlation, evaluated per ion on the ion's own D0. `StirredCell` (Sh = a (omega r^2/nu)^b Sc^c, k = Sh D/r; Bowen et al. 1997 defaults 0.23/0.567/0.33) needs `omega` and `radius`; `SchockMiquel` (a spacer channel) needs `velocity` and `hydraulicDiameter`. `viscosity` and `density` are REQUIRED (nu = mu/rho).

polarisation.title: Polarisation policy
polarisation.description: The film's POLICY, one block whichever way k arrives (a correlation or a bare `k_film`); declaring these words inside massTransfer {} refuses. `suctionCorrection`: GeraldesAfonso2006 (Xi = phi + (1 + 0.26 phi^1.4)^-1.7), filmTheory (the default: Xi = phi + phi/(e^phi - 1)) or none. `ionCoupling`: electroneutral (the multi-ionic model of Geraldes & Afonso 2007 -- each ion's k on its own D0, one interface potential gradient fixed by electroneutrality at the wall; needs >= 2 charged solutes) or none (the default, announced on an ion-declared feed).
